los.text: Answer a range of questions /ECG recognition/
los.html:
ECG to recogniseKey features
Normal sinus rhythmRegular, P before every QRS, rate 60–100
Atrial fibrillationIrregularly irregular, no P waves
Atrial flutterSawtooth flutter waves, often 2:1 (rate ~150)
SVTRegular narrow complex tachycardia, no visible P waves
VTBroad complex regular tachycardia
VFChaotic, no QRS: shockable arrest
STEMIST elevation in contiguous leads, reciprocal depression
Heart block1st: long PR; 2nd: dropped beats (Mobitz I lengthening PR; Mobitz II sudden); 3rd: P and QRS dissociated
HyperkalaemiaTall tented T, flat P, broad QRS

los.text: Explain the principles of Aseptic Non-Touch Technique (ANTT) and apply them appropriately during relevant clinical procedures to minimize the risk of infection
los.html:
ANTT principle
Hand hygiene at the right moments
Identify and protect key parts (anything that touches a sterile part or entry site) and key sites (wounds, insertion sites)
Non-touch technique for key parts
Standard ANTT (simple, short: general aseptic field, non-sterile gloves) vs surgical ANTT (complex, long: critical aseptic field, sterile gloves)
Clean equipment and a cleaned tray
Apply to: venepuncture, cannulation, blood cultures, IV drugs, catheters, wound care

los.text: Explain the clinical indications for performing a blood culture test.
los.html:
Indications
  • Suspected bacteraemia or sepsis (fever, rigors, hypothermia, NEWS2 rise with infection)
  • Endocarditis (3 sets from different sites over time)
  • Suspected line infection
  • Unexplained fever
  • Before antibiotics.
PurposeIdentify the organism and its sensitivities to target antibiotics.

los.text: Take a blood culture from a model while maintaining aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) principles.
los.html:
1Identity, explain, consent; hand hygiene; ANTT tray with aerobic and anaerobic bottles (check expiry), chlorhexidine/alcohol, blood culture collection set.
2Remove bottle caps and clean the tops with alcohol; allow to dry.
3Tourniquet, clean the skin for 30 s with 2% chlorhexidine/70% alcohol, let it dry, don't re-palpate.
4
  • Insert the butterfly
  • Fill aerobic first (when using a butterfly, to clear air from the tubing), then anaerobic: 8–10 mL per bottle (adults).
5Release the tourniquet, remove the needle, pressure, sharps away.
6Take other blood tubes after the cultures.
7Label at the bedside (not over the barcode), note site and time, send promptly; document.
  • Contamination (skin flora, e.g. coagulase-negative staph) leads to unnecessary antibiotics: hence strict ANTT.

los.text: Take a history from a non-communicative or minimally talkative patient using appropriate techniques.
los.html:
TechniquesOpen questions, comfortable silences, reflection, empathy, simple language; observe and comment gently; collateral history from family and notes.
In psychosis
  • The patient may be guarded, distracted by voices or suspicious
  • Don't argue with delusions
  • Stay calm and non-confrontational
  • Ensure safety (exit route).

los.text: Observe and interpret non-verbal communication cues during patient interactions.
los.html:
Cue in psychosisPossible meaning
Looking around, pausing as if listeningResponding to voices (auditory hallucinations)
Suspicious, guarded, evasiveParanoid delusions
Odd posture, mannerismsCatatonia, negative symptoms
Flat affect, poverty of speechNegative symptoms
AgitationRisk to self or others

los.text: Assess mental state by observing both objective and subjective features, including appearance, behaviour, and mood.
los.html:
• MSE (see ICM Year 1 › Mental health › LO 4): appearance and behaviour
    • speech
    • mood and affect
    • thought form and content
    • perception
    • cognition
    • insight
    • record objective observations separately from what the patient tells you (subjective).

los.text: Identify key symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions, and thought disorder.
los.html:
SymptomDefinition / example
HallucinationsPerception without a stimulus; auditory most common (third-person voices commenting = first-rank symptom)
DelusionsFixed, false beliefs out of keeping with culture, held despite evidence: persecutory, grandiose, reference, control
Thought disorderFormal thought disorder: loosening of associations, derailment, neologisms, word salad
Thought interferenceInsertion, withdrawal, broadcasting (first-rank)
Negative symptomsApathy, alogia, anhedonia, social withdrawal, blunted affect

los.text: Demonstrate awareness of safeguarding principles and apply them in scenarios involving potential risk or abuse.
los.html:
• Safeguarding: recognise risk or abuse (physical, sexual, emotional, financial, neglect, domestic, modern slavery), especially in vulnerable adults and children of patients
    • listen, don't promise secrecy, record facts, and report to the safeguarding lead/senior the same day.
    • Consider children at home when a parent is unwell.

los.text: Recognise and respond to patient cues related to self-harm and suicide, demonstrating appropriate communication and escalation.
los.html:
CueResponse
"I can't go on", "everyone would be better off without me"Ask directly about suicidal thoughts (asking doesn't increase risk)
Self-harm scars, giving away possessionsExplore gently
HopelessnessAsk about plans, means, preparations, protective factors (family, faith, pets)
Risk assessmentPrevious attempts, plans, access to means, alcohol/drugs, isolation, recent loss
EscalateTell a senior/supervisor; immediate risk → don't leave alone, crisis team / A&E; document
  • Respond with empathy: "Thank you for telling me; I can see how hard things are."
